subject: Helix Labs production: spikes of 504s and failed responses on Dedicated pool
messages:
From: Anya Li <anya@helixlabs.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@helixlabs.com
Date: 2026-11-01T08:17:00Z
Subject: Spike: 504s on Dedicated pool — Helix Labs production

Hi Evelyn,

We started seeing an increase in 504s and timeouts from our production workloads (dedicated pool: helix-prod-pool, region: us-west-2) starting ~07:55 UTC. Latency surged and token streams frequently terminated mid-response. Our app layer shows repeated "upstream closed" and the model API returned 503/504 fairly consistently for a subset of requests.

I've attached a tarball with request traces and server logs (helix_prod_504s_logs.tar.gz). Key facts we observed:
- Issue window: ~07:55–09:10 UTC (saw reduction after ~09:05).
- Affected routes: text-generation (gpt-j variants) and chat-stream.
- Error pattern: abrupt connection resets and OS-level socket errors reported by our infra.

Can you confirm whether this corresponds to anything on Redwood's side (node restarts, autoscale events, driver issues)? This is impacting SLAs for a handful of critical customers.

Appreciate a quick acknowledgement and any mitigation we can apply from our side.

Thanks,
Anya Li
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer
Helix Labs

Attachments: helix_prod_504s_logs.tar.gz

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Anya Li <anya@helixlabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike: 504s on Dedicated pool — Helix Labs production

Hi Anya — thanks for the quick flag. We saw correlated alerts for increased OOMs and pod restarts in the dedicated pool for your tenant around the same time. I'm escalating to our infra team (cc'd).

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Temporarily increased per-tenant concurrency cap on your pool to reduce head-of-line blocking.
- Enabled a conservative autoscale override to allow faster scale-up for the next 60 minutes.
- Collecting GPU driver logs + kernel messages from affected nodes — please hold off on any changes while we collect evidence.

We'll follow up within the hour with a root-cause hypothesis and short-term mitigation. Sorry for the disruption — we'll prioritize this.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (runbook excerpt attached inline)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Li <anya@helixlabs.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike: 504s on Dedicated pool — Helix Labs production

Hi all — investigating and bouncing logs now. Preliminary technical summary:

What we're seeing
- Multiple GPU hosts (n=3) in helix-prod-pool had repeated driver-level GPU memory leaks on driver version 515.86.x. This caused the GPU process to OOM and the node to mark the inference runtime unhealthy -> pod evictions.
- The cluster autoscaler had a config mismatch: readiness probes for the inference runtime timed out quickly under heavy kernel-level stalls, marking nodes NotReady before the scale-up hook could provision replacements. The autoscaler then deferred scale-up due to a conservative cooldown/regression detector that treated the transient failures as flapping, so provisioning lagged.
- Result: short window where available GPU capacity dropped below your concurrent request footprint leading to request termination and 504s.

Immediate mitigations performed (complete)
- Rolled a targeted GPU driver restart on the 3 affected hosts to reclaim memory and avoid full reboots (recovery at 09:12 UTC).
- Temporarily loosened the autoscaler cooldown and increased desired capacity by 20% for helix-prod-pool to absorb surge.
- Pushed a small autoscaler-config-diff.patch to the cluster controller to adjust readiness timeout thresholds and disable the flap detector for this pool.

Next actions (short timeline)
- We will deploy a driver-level patch (vendor recommended) to all nodes in the pool overnight (ETA start: 2026-11-02 02:00 UTC). Attachment: gpu_heapdump_11-01.bin contains a truncated heap dump for vendor triage.
- We'll coordinate a rolling node upgrade with Helix (expected disruption: minimal; we will keep concurrency caps and can schedule a maintenance window if you prefer full isolation).
- Postmortem and remediation plan will be shared by 2026-11-05.

Customer impact and compensation
- We acknowledge this affected SLA for Helix Labs during the incident window. Evelyn, can we offer a one-time service credit; suggested amount 5% of November committed capacity invoice?

Notes for ops: retaining all kernel logs, container logs, autoscaler traces in INF-8423.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: gpu_heapdump_11-01.bin, autoscaler-config-diff.patch

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Anya Li <anya@helixlabs.com>, ops@helixlabs.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:00:00Z
Subject: Redwood update: helix-prod-pool incident and next steps

Hi Anya and team —

Thanks again for flagging this morning and for the fast signal sharing. Below is a concise incident update and our commitments.

Summary
- Incident window: 2026-11-01T07:55:00Z — 2026-11-01T09:12:00Z (partial recovery observed after targeted driver restarts).
- Root cause: GPU driver memory leak on driver 515.86.x combined with an autoscaler readiness timeout + flap-detection config that delayed scale-up.
- Impact: a subset of requests against your dedicated pool returned 503/504 during the window.

Actions we've completed
- Immediate driver restarts and temporary capacity increase to stabilize traffic.
- Autoscaler config change applied to the pool to prevent premature node eviction under kernel stalls.
- Full evidence (logs, heap dump, autoscaler traces) gathered and attached to JIRA INF-8423.

Planned work and timelines
- Vendor driver patch rollout (all nodes in helix-prod-pool): start 2026-11-02 02:00 UTC, expected complete 2026-11-02 06:00 UTC. We will do a rolling upgrade and expect no more than brief reconnections; we will keep you updated.
- Full postmortem (root cause analysis, long-term mitigations, and code/config changes): delivered by 2026-11-05.

Compensation
- We will apply a one-time 5% service credit for November pro-rated to the incident window. If you'd like to escalate this amount to your procurement team, please let me know and I'll route for approvals.

Action items for Helix Labs (requested)
- Please confirm whether you want the rolling maintenance to occur in the stated overnight window or if you require a different maintenance window.
- Provide any additional traces you prefer we preserve beyond what's already in INF-8423.

I'll be the primary contact for customer communications; Marissa will coordinate billing/credits and Karthik will lead the engineering remediation.

Apologies for the disruption — we know the reliability bar must be higher. We will follow up with the full postmortem and an ops playbook to avoid recurrence.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: helix_prod_504s_logs.tar.gz, gpu_heapdump_11-01.bin, autoscaler-config-diff.patch
